stories.title: Indonesian Ferry Capsizes in Java Sea, About 130 Missing
stories.summary: Indonesian rescuers said Sunday that about 130 passengers and crew are missing after the ferry Virgo Transport 8, carrying more than 240 people, capsized and sank in rough seas in the Java Sea while traveling from Surabaya to Banjarmasin. The captain had reported waves up to 3 meters before issuing a distress call saying the ship was listing; contact was lost around 2 a.m. Sunday. By Sunday afternoon, search teams backed by a navy vessel and a helicopter had rescued 107 people and recovered six bodies. The ship's manifest listed 243 people aboard, though passenger counts often differ from official figures in Indonesia.

stories.title: Iraq Seizes Drone-Launch Platform Tied to Saudi Pipeline Attack
stories.summary: Iraqi security forces said Saturday they located and seized a drone-launching platform used in a September 11 attack that struck Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, Iraq's Security Media Cell said. Saudi authorities traced the launch site to Maysan province in southeastern Iraq near the Iranian border; the strikes injured several people and prompted Saudi Arabia to shut the pipeline, which carries about 4-5% of global oil supply and lets the kingdom bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Iraq's prime minister reshuffled military commanders in the border region, and the Maysan operations commander and provincial police chief were dismissed and are under investigation. Saudi Arabia said it will not retaliate for now, at Baghdad's request.

stories.title: Iran, Gulf States Set for Rare Hormuz Talks as Tanker Struck Near Qeshm
stories.summary: An Iranian cargo vessel was struck early Sunday off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one person and wounding four, Iranian state media reported, a day before foreign ministers from Iran, Iraq and Gulf states are due to meet in Oman to discuss managing shipping through the strait. The meeting would be the first to bring Gulf Cooperation Council states and Iran together since the war began in February, centered on an Iran-Oman framework under which vessels would pay fees for safe transit; only Iraq has confirmed attendance so far, while Bahrain says it will not attend. Commercial traffic through Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil supply, remains depressed, and oil prices have risen again after Houthi forces seized territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast. Iran has said it will only fully reopen the waterway if the United States ends its naval blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Anthropic Says China-Based AI Labs Ran Large-Scale Claude Distillation Campaigns
stories.summary: Anthropic said this week it detected and disrupted large-scale unauthorized efforts by China-based AI labs, including Alibaba, Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, Xiaomi and Zhipu, to train their own models on outputs from its Claude models, a practice known as distillation. The company said the combined activity totaled nearly 200 million exchanges, with more than 151 million attributed to Alibaba between May and July and over 12 million to DeepSeek over 14 days in July, much of it routed through networks of thousands of fraudulent accounts. Anthropic said Moonshot AI relayed almost 300,000 customer requests to Claude over 10 days via a proxy network, and that some exchanges exposed sensitive information from individual users, companies and state-affiliated actors. China has rejected the accusations.

stories.title: New Supernova Catalogue Adds to Evidence That Dark Energy May Be Changing
stories.summary: An international team led by the University of Queensland published the largest-ever catalogue of Type Ia supernovae, compiling data on 2,884 exploding white dwarf stars by unifying three decades of observations with the Dark Energy Survey and other cosmological datasets. The analysis, led by PhD candidate Ryan Camilleri, found evidence that dark energy's influence may not be constant over cosmic history as assumed under the standard model of cosmology, but could instead change over time. The findings align with earlier hints from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and James Webb Space Telescope data, though researchers caution the supernova catalogue alone remains statistically consistent with no time evolution and the work has not completed peer review. The results were detailed in a paper submitted to the Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia.

stories.title: Death Toll Rises to 26 in Fire and Stampede at DR Congo School
stories.summary: At least 26 children died and 25 were injured in a fire and stampede at a primary school in Bukavu, in the M23-controlled eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, UNICEF said, after blazes broke out simultaneously at three locations about 500 meters apart on the morning of September 10. A teacher described students jumping from upper floors to escape as the wooden school building burned; a Congolese education ministry report said students were trampled in the stampede and those trapped inside died of asphyxiation. M23 declared three days of mourning, and funerals for the 20 girls and six boys killed were held Saturday. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
